analysis: This PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/direct-mode.md (head lines 48-54) and docs/reference/configuration.md (new row at head line 413). It documents a load-time "shape warmup" for standalone `--local` preload, controlled by `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP`. The documented behavior is a short shader-cache probe, then shape cells only after a new install or a macOS/MLX kernel update. The warmup is time-bounded (20 s per engine). It is described as training no rate or counter, and as preempted by incoming requests. No code, auth, attestation, encryption, key-handling or coordinator-wire behavior changes in the supplied evidence. No change touches TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 controls, or the T-041 prefix-cache controls (HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, account scoping, SEC-035 acceptance). The variable is described as read from ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift and "Forwarded to the LaunchAgent". That implies a LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys addition, which is not in this batch. If it ships, it is a benign performance toggle that gates no security control. The warmup runs synthetic prompts, not consumer data, so A-001 exposure is unchanged. Warmup before the listener opens, and sweep-tick warmup when idle, could in theory add a small availability or timing surface (T-029 class). The docs state that requests preempt it and that the 20 s bound applies, but I could not verify this against the implementation. The claims in the docs (LaunchAgent forwarding, ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmupMode, 20 s bound, preemption) are unverified contracts, because no code is supplied. They are not evidence of a regression. The patch excerpt for configuration.md is truncated, but the changed range map is complete (single line at 413). No threat-model update is needed for this docs-only change.
